extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community and applicants preparing NIH grant proposals (investigators, administrators, small businesses)
extracted.subtask_description: High-level guidance and policy updates relevant to preparing and understanding NIH extramural applications, reviews, data-sharing plans, and program opportunities. Summarizes recent NIH news items applicants should consider when preparing submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate experimental models (NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions; NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches and encourages approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use models that are scientifically sound and best fit the research question. New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) are supported when they improve human relevance/translational potential, but choice should be driven by appropriateness to the question rather than novelty for its own sake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award should follow the PF5 award structure and application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview for key features, required application format, and procedural notes (for example, how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests). Be prepared that an application could be split into linked awards post-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH issued a 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS Plans, use the new pilot format and include the simplified set of required elements specified by NIH for 2026. This is an official format and replaces/augments previous expectations for DMS content for pilots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility in applications and awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliability of biomedical research is foundational; NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan and a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative encourage embedding replication and reproducibility throughout NIH research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate design, methods, and plans that support replication and reproducibility into applications and conduct of awards. Expect replication/reproducibility to be a highlighted topic and an incentivized institutional priority; consider addressing these explicitly in proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'Competitive But Not Discussed' review outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Following emergency modifications, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed' — recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your application receives a 'competitive but not discussed' designation, understand this reflects a middle-third placement in study-section ranking under the temporary or modified review cutoffs; it does not necessarily indicate a weak application. Use this context when deciding next steps (resubmission, inquiries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness of centralized NIH peer review changes
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH centralized peer review within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency; applicants should be aware of consolidation effects on peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect procedural and possibly substantive changes in how applications are handled and reviewed due to centralization. Applicants should monitor NIH communications about consolidated peer-review processes and any implications for study-section assignment, review timelines, or evaluation criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Seed Fund / Small Business Program availability
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH’s Small Business Program (Seed Fund) has resumed operations; this is important news for innovators, founders, and R&D-driven small companies seeking NIH small-business funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small business applicants and startups should note the program’s return and check NIH channels for current solicitations, eligibility, and application procedures (SBIR/STTR-related guidance will be posted on relevant NIH pages).
